claim_verdicts.evidence: Arithmetic: (90*5 + 10*500)/100 = 54.5 ms, so 'about 55 ms' (section 4) and 'about 50 ms' (section 6) both hold; 500/54.5 = 9.2, 'about ten times'. Histograms and summaries: a phi-quantile is the observation at rank phi*N; 0.95*100 = 95th, positions 91-100 are 500 ms, so p95 = 500 ms.

Histograms and summaries (WebFetch summary, round 1): a phi-quantile is the observation value at rank phi*N among N observations; the 0.95-quantile is the 95th percentile, so 95% of observations are at or below it. Lesson section 3 ('at or below' / 'took at most'), section 4 and summary line 2 now match this wording and the worked example.

Metric types, Histogram: "cumulative counters for the observation buckets, exposed as <basename>_bucket{le="<upper inclusive bound>"}", "the total sum of all observed values, exposed as <basename>_sum", "the count of events that have been observed, exposed as <basename>_count (identical to <basename>_bucket{le="+Inf"} above)"; buckets are cumulative, "every bucket counts all observations less than or equal to the upper boundary".

Histograms and summaries: rate(http_request_duration_seconds_sum[5m]) / rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count[5m]) gives the average request duration over the last 5 minutes. Metric types: _sum and _count are cumulative; a counter's value "can only increase or be reset to zero on restart", so raw _sum/_count is the average since the process started.
